samples.summary: URL construction for the api-keys management routes is duplicated in the command layer instead of reused from HttpClient. `apiKeysUrl()` re-derives `${server}/workspaces/${seg(workspace)}/api-keys[/:id]`, which HttpClient already builds in three places (listApiKeys/createApiKey/revokeApiKey). The whole point of the change is that "the preview is the request", yet the preview now depends on a hand-copied mirror that can silently drift (e.g. if the route ever moves under /api/v1). A single exported URL builder on HttpClient (or a dry-run mode on the client) would make the guarantee structural rather than by comment.

samples.summary: `seg()` is defined twice — exported from `client/dry-run.ts` and again as a private copy in `client/http-client.ts` — for the same one-line `encodeURIComponent` wrapper whose entire justification is that both sides must agree. Two definitions is the wrong shape for a helper that exists to keep two call sites identical; it belongs in one shared module (e.g. `client/url.ts`) imported by both. It also leaves `http-client.ts:270` (`downloadFileDocument`) still calling `encodeURIComponent` directly, so there are now three encodings of the same idea.
samples.evidence: packages/cli/src/client/dry-run.ts:12 `export function seg` and packages/cli/src/client/http-client.ts:32 `function seg` are byte-identical bodies

samples.summary: Layering: non-dry-run modules now import a URL-encoding helper from `client/dry-run.ts` (`docs/import.ts`, `notes/import.ts`, `slides/import.ts`). A path-segment encoder is a client/URL concern, not a dry-run-printer concern; importing the dry-run module for it couples the import pipelines to the preview printer.

The endpoint-selection logic of `HttpClient.getCells`/`getCell` (range-vs-single-ref, and `?range=` encoding) is re-implemented in the dry-run branches of `cells.ts` and again in `sheets-export.ts`. Three copies of the same routing rule must stay in sync for the preview to remain truthful; the routing could live once in the client (e.g. a path-building function the client and preview both call).
samples.evidence: cells.ts: `const base = `/documents/${seg(docId)}/tabs/${seg(tab)}/cells`; const path = range?.includes(':') ? ... ` mirrored in sheets-export.ts:45-52 and http-client.ts:358-365

samples.summary: Unrelated scope creep: the change to the CI lane-selection test (`resolve fail-safes`, adding GITHUB_EVENT_NAME/GITHUB_REF_NAME and a `push to main` assertion) has nothing to do with CLI dry-run coverage or URL-segment encoding. It may well be a correct fix, but it belongs in its own change; bundled here it makes the CLI-behaviour change harder to review and to revert.

The new design-doc paragraph overstates completeness: "The one command the flag does not hold back is `login`". `ctx switch` (writes the session file / switches active workspace) and `logout` also ignore `--dry-run` and mutate local state. Either qualify the claim to network requests only, or list the local-state commands as exceptions.

finding.summary: URL construction for the api-keys management routes is duplicated in the command layer instead of reused from HttpClient. `apiKeysUrl()` re-derives `${server}/workspaces/${seg(workspace)}/api-keys[/:id]`, which HttpClient already builds in three places (listApiKeys/createApiKey/revokeApiKey). The whole point of the change is that "the preview is the request", yet the preview now depends on a hand-copied mirror that can silently drift (e.g. if the route ever moves under /api/v1). A single exported URL builder on HttpClient (or a dry-run mode on the client) would make the guarantee structural rather than by comment.
finding.evidence: function apiKeysUrl(opts, keyId?) { const base = `${server}/workspaces/${seg(config.workspace)}/api-keys`; ... } — duplicating http-client.ts lines ~404-417

verdict.reason: The claimed code is present verbatim: packages/cli/src/commands/api-keys.ts:13-18 defines apiKeysUrl() building `${server}/workspaces/${seg(config.workspace)}/api-keys[/${seg(keyId)}]`, a hand-copied mirror of the identical construction repeated three times in packages/cli/src/client/http-client.ts:397-421 (listApiKeys L398-399, createApiKey L405-406, revokeApiKey L416-417). HttpClient exposes no URL builder for these non-v1 routes (its private `base` getter at L98-101 covers only /api/v1) and no dry-run mode, so the preview's correctness rests only on the comment at api-keys.ts:7-12 telling maintainers to keep the mirror in sync. No guard makes this unreachable: http-client-paths.test.ts:76-82 pins only the client-side URL, and read-dry-run.test.ts only asserts the client method is not called — nothing asserts preview URL == request URL. Duplication/reuse is explicitly inside this lens's lane, and the task doc (docs/tasks/active/20260816-cli-dry-run-read-commands-todo.md:41-48) makes "the preview stays the request" the guarantee at stake, while its Non-goals (L50-54) do not exclude an exported builder. The only debatable point is whether duplicating a URL template rather than a whole module is major or a minor refactor preference — that ambiguity is not a named refutation ground, so the finding stands.

finding.summary: New doc bullet asserts a global invariant ("Identifiers are URL-encoded into the previewed path exactly as the client encodes them") that the import/upload previews do not satisfy
finding.evidence: cli.md:836-841 states the encoding invariant unconditionally, and 824-830 claims "A dry run never reaches the network" across the CLI. But the import previews were left untouched by this change: packages/cli/src/docs/import.ts:155 prints `path: `/documents/${replace}/content`` with a RAW, unencoded id (same in slides/import.ts:177+, notes/import.ts:142+, files/upload.ts:171). Those previews also emit a different envelope — `{ method, path, body }` with no `dry_run: true` and no absolute `url` — so they neither go through `printDryRun` nor honour the documented shape shown at cli.md:813-820. The change hardened and documented one half of the dry-run surface while the doc speaks for all of it.

verdict.reason: The claimed evidence is not present in the repository. docs/import.ts:158, notes/import.ts:150 and slides/import.ts:185 all interpolate the id via `seg(replace)` (imported from ../client/dry-run.js), and `seg` is `encodeURIComponent` (client/dry-run.ts:12-14), the same encoder HttpClient uses (http-client.ts:32) — not a raw id as the finding states. files/upload.ts:176 prints `path: '/files'` with no interpolated identifier. The doc's encoding invariant (cli.md:838-841) therefore holds for the import/upload previews. The envelope difference the finding says is undocumented is explicitly documented at cli.md:844-848 ("The `import` / `upload` previews are the one envelope variation... The identifier encoding is the same."), so cli.md:813-820 is not asserted as universal. The "no network" claim also holds: each dryRun branch returns before any client call (docs/import.ts:153-164, notes/import.ts:143-158, slides/import.ts:178-194).
